statements.text: Every dotfiles-ai full apply checks and converges the latest compatible stable OpenCode release on the host and all registered managed guests.
Use official OpenCode release assets and published SHA-256 digests on every platform; Homebrew formula state is not runtime authority.
Stage and validate one candidate everywhere before guest-then-host activation; rollback or durable commit recovery prevents fleet divergence.
Update activation never signals or restarts current OpenCode or Herdr processes; only later launches use the replacement inode.
A healthy fleet retains its verified release when metadata, download, validation, or a target is unavailable; unhealthy bootstrap and rollback failure remain nonzero.
Preserve OpenCode XDG state, sessions, providers, credentials, configuration, and current process state without inspection or copying across boundaries.

Validate version, help, resolved managed configuration, native role discovery, skills and required DBSCTR CLI operations before activation; the approved replacement retires redundant custom DBSCTR tool catalogs.
OpenCode CLI/config contracts can drift on stable releases; incompatible candidates are rejected by canonical full-candidate digest and never activated.

Migrate Fedora guests from the delivered root-owned OpenCode binary to the user-local managed path; retain the root binary only as first-migration rollback authority and retire provisioning after fleet validation.

Migrate the host, every registered managed guest and supported provisioning and CI profiles to V2; the prior guest deferral is lifted for this migration, while additional unregistered machines remain excluded.
Include CLI and Desktop and qualify shared configuration, data, services and external-state-root behavior.

Use a separately approved controlled major-version migration window, preserving native conversation identity, provider affinity, worktree selection and writer authority; ordinary rolling updates retain their no-restart contract.
Prefer native V2 conversion with an immutable original archive and reviewed transformation report; retain existing recovery evidence and never discard post-cutover V2 work during rollback.
Report functional gaps with impact, safe unavailable behavior, owner and review condition for later reconciliation; perfect V1 feature parity is not required and no blanket gate exception is granted.
Unexplained message loss, incorrect authorization and unsafe recovery block activation; qualify native interfaces before declaring implementation readiness.
Retire V1 active launch, update, provisioning and CI paths after fleet verification; keep inactive recovery material until separately reviewed disposal without rewriting historical evidence.
Preserve boundary-local credentials and history throughout rehearsal and deployment; never copy host state into guests as an upgrade shortcut.
Extend this initiative using the approved lifecycle, OpenCode control-plane and distribution contexts; serialize shared ownership and preserve unrelated relocation work.

Provide a repeatable checksum-bound isolated V2 CLI surface probe with bounded subprocesses and sanitized results; surface success must never imply continuation, migration or deployment qualification.

Implement read-only V2 native actor and message-qualified terminal-proof compatibility from observed schema contracts; reject stale V1 fallback, incomplete conversion, ambiguous calls and background completion while preserving V1 and Codex regression behavior.

Stock V2 direct custom-tool ask is not an authorization boundary. The approved native-workspace replacement retires that lifecycle transport; use native built-in permissions and enforced CLI validation, preserve bounded private projections, and keep unsupported identity-dependent capabilities unavailable. Source controls are specified; deployment still requires affected native permission and integration gates.
Adopt Worktrunk-managed sibling repository.worktrees containers and native worktree sessions; broad-root sessions coordinate and navigate rather than transparently route implementation.
Use a repository-scoped external DVC cache, code-only worktree creation, targeted reflink materialization and coordinated cache retention; no silent large-data copy fallback or automatic full pull.
Keep primary checkout paths and branches stable, scope agent searches explicitly, and isolate independent writers in separate worktrees while retaining reviewed PR delivery.

Review keep/replace/retire contracts before removing continuation or relocation behavior; preserve existing dirty worktrees, caches, cycle authority and conversations during individually verified migration.

Worktrunk replaces custom DBSCTR allocation and management, with no permanent legacy allocator or fallback; DBSCTR operates in the explicit native checkout and retains evidence gates rather than worktree orchestration.

Use dbsctrctl through native shell permissions and retire redundant custom tool wrappers; report unavailable native message/call attribution truthfully without treating caller-supplied metadata as authentication.
Replace task-worktree orchestration for both OpenCode and Codex CLI while preserving native sandbox, permissions, provider affinity, credential/state boundaries and unrelated history capabilities.

After pausing writers, adopt existing worktrees in place and continue original cycles, preserving identities, dirty work, failed gates and uncertain operation evidence; relocation and cache consolidation remain separate operations.
Use a small launch-time busy check with explicit operator override, not writer leases or per-tool admission; disclose direct-launch, in-UI-switching and background-work limitations.

Replace wrapper-only Initiative approval with explicit interactive CLI confirmation of the fresh launch digest. Refuse noninteractive registration, recheck authority after confirmation, and keep native permission enforcement and unavailable actor attribution distinct from operator confirmation.

Defer hourly OpenCode and Codex updates, automatic idle service upgrades and independently advancing fleet update policy until after the one-time V2 transition; update automation is not a migration prerequisite.

Complete a one-time transition to the latest official stable OpenCode V2 selected at staging. Bind the migration attempt to verified candidate bytes, qualify synthetic then boundary-local real-history conversion and recovery, perform operator-assisted UI checks, and use a bounded maintenance cutover before admitting normal work.

Accept the reviewed native incomplete-compaction and malformed-record omissions and external-attachment placeholders while retaining complete original history and separately archiving available referenced regular files. Current file snapshots are recovery aids, not proven historical attachment bytes; unexpected loss remains a blocker.

Continue the one-time V2 transition through verified live completion and merge passing approved transition pull requests instead of stopping at draft delivery. Exact slice launch consent, enforced permission boundaries, qualified maintenance and preservation requirements remain mandatory.
